sections.heading: ADULT CARDIAC ARREST
sections.content:
[b]Emergency & Critical Care[/b]
Guideline basis: 2025 American Heart Association (AHA) Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

sections.heading: RECOGNIZE CARDIAC ARREST
sections.content:
Suspect cardiac arrest when an adult patient is:
• Unresponsive.
• Not breathing normally (apnea or agonal gasping).
• Without a definite central pulse.

[b]Pulse check:[/b] Check carotid or femoral pulse for no more than 10 seconds.

[b]Immediate action:[/b]
• Activate the resuscitation/code team.
• Start high-quality CPR immediately.
• Attach monitor/defibrillator as soon as available.
• Do not delay CPR for ECG, investigations, or IV access.

sections.heading: HIGH-QUALITY CPR
sections.content:
[b]Chest compressions:[/b]
• Rate: 100–120 compressions/min.
• Depth: At least 5 cm (2 inches), avoiding excessive depth.
• Allow complete chest recoil.
• Minimize interruptions; pauses should be less than 10 seconds.
• Change compressor approximately every 2 minutes or sooner if fatigued.

[b]Defibrillation Energy:[/b]
• Biphasic: 120–200 J.
• Monophasic: 360 J.

sections.heading: DRUG THERAPY (SHOCKABLE)
sections.content:
[b]1. Epinephrine (Adrenaline)[/b]
• Dose: 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes.

[b]2. Amiodarone[/b]
• First dose: 300 mg IV/IO bolus.
• Second dose: 150 mg IV/IO if VF/pVT persists.

sections.heading: REVERSIBLE CAUSES: Hs AND Ts
sections.content:
[b]Hs:[/b] Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Acidosis, Hypo/Hyperkalemia, Hypothermia.
[b]Ts:[/b] Tension pneumothorax, Cardiac tamponade, Toxins, Pulmonary thrombosis, Coronary thrombosis.

sections.heading: ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME (ACS)
sections.content:
[b]Emergency & Critical Care[/b]
Evidence-based clinical approach based on the 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline and 2023 ESC Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DEFINITION AND CLASSIFICATION
sections.content:
ACS is a spectrum of clinical conditions caused by acute myocardial ischemia, most commonly due to disruption or erosion of an atherosclerotic coronary plaque with superimposed thrombosis.

[b]ACS includes:[/b]
• [b]STEMI:[/b] Acute myocardial infarction with persistent ST-segment elevation.
• [b]NSTEMI:[/b] Acute myocardial infarction without persistent ST elevation, characterized by a rise and/or fall in cardiac troponin.
• [b]Unstable Angina (UA):[/b] Acute myocardial ischemia without evidence of acute myocardial injury.

sections.heading: 4. INITIAL ASSESSMENT & IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
sections.content:
[b]Immediate management:[/b]
• Assess ABCs and place on continuous cardiac monitoring.
• Obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately (ideally within 10 minutes).
• Establish IV access, measure vitals, and obtain blood samples (hs-cTn).
• [b]Do not delay reperfusion in clear STEMI while waiting for troponin results.[/b]

sections.heading: 6. ASPIRIN
sections.content:
[b]Dose:[/b]
• Loading dose: 162–325 mg orally, preferably chewed.
• Maintenance dose: 75–100 mg orally once daily.

sections.heading: 20. CARDIOGENIC SHOCK
sections.content:
[b]Suspect when:[/b] Persistent hypotension, need for vasopressors, altered mental status, oliguria, cold extremities, elevated lactate.

[b]Management:[/b]
• Activate cardiogenic shock team, urgent echo, emergency angiography/revascularization.
• [b]Norepinephrine:[/b] 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min IV (Target MAP ≥65 mmHg).

sections.heading: 01 — DEFINITION
sections.content: Nephritic syndrome is a clinical presentation of glomerular inflammation characterized by hematuria, dysmorphic red blood cells or red-cell casts, reduced kidney function in some patients, hypertension, and variable proteinuria.

sections.heading: 02 — RECOGNIZE
sections.content:
- Dark, tea-colored, or cola-colored urine.
- Microscopic or visible hematuria.
- Periorbital or peripheral edema.
- Hypertension, sometimes severe.
- Oliguria or reduced urine output.
- Elevated serum creatinine.

sections.heading: 04 — IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
sections.content:
- Assess ABCs, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and volume status.
- Check urine output and obtain urgent renal function and electrolyte measurements.
- Look for hypertensive emergency, pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, or uremic complications.
- Obtain urinalysis and urine microscopy.

sections.heading: NEPHROTIC SYNDROME
sections.content: [b]Internal Medicine & Nephrology[/b]

sections.heading: DEFINITION
sections.content:
A clinical disorder caused by increased glomerular permeability to plasma proteins, resulting in significant urinary protein loss.

[b]Diagnostic features:[/b]
• Heavy proteinuria: ≥3.5 g/24 hours in adults.
• Hypoalbuminemia: commonly serum albumin <3.0 g/dL.
• Peripheral edema.
• Hyperlipidemia and lipiduria.

sections.heading: MANAGEMENT: EDEMA
sections.content:
[b]Dietary sodium restriction:[/b] ~2 g/day (about 5 g salt).
[b]Fluid restriction:[/b] Not routinely required. Consider in severe edema, hyponatremia, or fluid overload.

[b]Loop diuretics (First-line):[/b]
• Furosemide: 20–40 mg PO once/twice daily. IV: 20–40 mg IV (adjust per response).

sections.heading: TETANUS
sections.content:
[b]Emergency Medicine & Critical Care[/b]
Life-threatening neurological disease caused by tetanospasmin, a neurotoxin produced by Clostridium tetani.

sections.heading: RECOGNIZE TETANUS (CLINICAL FEATURES)
sections.content:
[b]Typical features:[/b]
• Trismus (lockjaw) - inability to open the mouth.
• Neck stiffness, dysphagia, difficulty swallowing.
• Generalized muscle rigidity.
• Painful muscle spasms triggered by light, sound, or touch.
• Risus sardonicus (facial grimacing).

sections.heading: 3. ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY
sections.content:
[b]Preferred: Metronidazole[/b]
• Dose: 500 mg IV every 6–8 hours.
• Duration: 7–10 days.

[b]Important:[/b] Antibiotics reduce further toxin production. They do NOT neutralize toxin already produced.

sections.heading: RABIES
sections.content:
[b]Emergency Medicine & Infectious Diseases[/b]
Acute, progressive viral encephalitis caused by rabies virus, a member of the Lyssavirus genus. Usually transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected mammal, particularly dogs.

sections.heading: MANAGEMENT: PART A (PEP) - VACCINE
sections.content:
[b]Essen regimen:[/b]
• Day 0: First dose.
• Day 3: Second dose.
• Day 7: Third dose.
• Day 14: Fourth dose.

[b]Dose:[/b] 1 mL IM per dose for commonly used HDCV or PCECV vaccines.

sections.heading: DIPHTHERIA
sections.content:
[b]Emergency Medicine & Infectious Diseases[/b]
Acute, potentially life-threatening bacterial infection caused by toxin-producing Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

sections.heading: RECOGNIZE: RESPIRATORY DIPHTHERIA
sections.content:
[b]Characteristic pseudomembrane:[/b]
• Gray or dirty-white appearance.
• Firmly adherent to underlying tissue.
• Bleeds when forcibly removed.
• May extend from tonsils to pharynx, larynx, or nasal cavity.

[b]WARNING:[/b] Never attempt forceful removal of the pseudomembrane.
